function: CSI feedback: gradient-based NAS generates the RefineNet cell of the BS-side decoder that reconstructs CSI from a randomly projected, quantized codeword, customized per scenario (p. 2, 6).
system: FDD massive MIMO-OFDM, BS with 32-antenna ULA, single-antenna UE, 512 or 1024 subcarriers; QuaDRiGa 2.655 GHz, COST2100 5.3 GHz indoor and 300 MHz outdoor; no RIS (p. 10).
method: PC-DARTS gradient-based neural architecture search (MSE reconstruction loss, bilevel optimization, weight sharing) with early stopping and elastic selection; candidate cells retrained from scratch per dataset (p. 8, 9).
data_channel: COST2100 indoor and outdoor datasets published by [13] (150,000 samples) and QuaDRiGa 3GPP 38.901 UMi LOS and NLOS scenarios (100,000 samples) simulated by the authors (p. 10).
test_conditions: Search, training and testing within each of four datasets; sweeps of CR 1/4 to 1/64 and 4, 8, 32 quantization bits; no cross-scenario test (p. 10, 12).
baselines: Manually designed learned networks CS-CsiNet, CS-CsiNet+, CS-CRNet, CS-MRFNet, and CS-SimpleCNN; no non-learned method is compared (p. 10, 13).
metrics: NMSE in dB; average spectral efficiency with zero-forcing precoding; cell FLOPs and running time per sample; search cost in GPU days (p. 9, 10, 12).
complexity: Table V: cell FLOPs 0.90 to 6.07 M for Auto-CsiNet-N1 to N6, 1.62 to 7.78 M for manual cells; runtime 0.046 to 0.050 s per sample (p. 12).
openness: COST2100 channel dataset published by [13] is used (p. 10); authors give no code or link.
q1_support: p. 10: "3GPP-38.901-UMi-LOS 3GPP-38.901-UMi-NLOS" - scenarios of the QuaDRiGa datasets in Table III; the COST2100 indoor and outdoor datasets are also used.
q2_support: p. 13: "are searched on the QuaDRiGa Scene 1/2 and COST2100 Indoor/Outdoor tasks" - each scenario gets its own search and training and its own test split; the CR and quantization-bit results (p. 12, Tables V and VI) use retrained networks, so no trained model is tested in a new scenario.
q3_support: p. 10: "Auto-CsiNet with that of CS-CsiNet [13], CS-CsiNet+ [23]," plus CS-CRNet and CS-MRFNet; all are learned networks, and no non-learned method (compressed sensing recovery or codebook) is compared in the experiments.
q4_support: p. 12: "practical running time per sample, tested on a Tesla" - Table V also lists cell complexity in FLOPs, 0.90 to 6.07 M for Auto-CsiNet-N1 to N6.
q5_support: p. 1: "COST2100 indoor/outdoor scene dataset (released by [13])" - the published COST2100 channel dataset is used for training and testing (also p. 10); the authors release no code or link.
notes: Included, area 2: NAS (PC-DARTS) designs the decoder of a CS-CsiNet CSI feedback network per scenario (p. 2, 6). q2 is borderline: p. 12 claims generalization over CR and quantization bits, but each network is retrained. q3 not met: only manually designed learned networks are compared (p. 10). q5 rests on the published COST2100 dataset.
